To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of high temperature and higher solid loads was the most significant factor affecting final ethanol concentration, whereas solid and hydrothermal liquor loadings had more significant impact on ethanol productivities.

the selection of an appropriate industrial strain along with nutritional supplements and process optimization enabled to produce high ethanol titers under restrictive conditions (e.g., high solid loadings) that can reduce operating cost, and boost the economic viability of lignocellulosics to ethanol processes.

the combination of higher temperatures and solid loadings was detrimental to ethanol productivity, but the addition of a high percentage of autohydrolyzed liquid fraction (containing inhibitors) was the main variable influencing the final ethanol concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust and cost-effective SSF strategy to produce ethanol from lignocellulosics.
the development of a robust and low-cost lignocellulosics-to-ethanol process.

the optimization of SSF process performance using an industrial strain of S. cerevisiae in a wide range of operating conditions, which are representative of those encountered in industrial lignocelluloses-to-ethanol bioprocesses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of a high temperature (37 °C), 60 % autohydrolysis liquid, and 16 g of solid (liquid to solid of 6.3 g/g), is the most suitable operating condition to achieve the maximum ethanol concentration and productivity.
the combination of different operating stresses can be used to improve ethanol productivity and reduce process costs.

the combined effect of temperature and solid loadings is the main factor affecting final ethanol production in SSF processes, whereas the liquid to solid ratio and autohydrolyzed liquor loadings are the main factors affecting ethanol productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the selection of a suitable yeast strain, the addition of nutrients and the use of hydrothermal pretreatment are key factors to obtain a robust process that is capable to produce high titers of bioethanol under multiple stresses conditions.

the selection of an adequate industrial strain, the use of autohydrolyzed liquor, and the optimization of operating conditions can reduce the operating costs of lignocellulosics-to-ethanol process, thus increasing the economic viability of the process.
the combination of autohydrolyzed liquor and high solid load is a suitable approach to increase ethanol concentration in SSF processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of high temperature and high solid load can be used as a tool to improve the performance of lignocellulosics bioethanol production processes.
the use of a robust industrial yeast strain and the supplementation with low-cost nutrients derived from the agro-food industry can improve the performance of SSF under multiple stress conditions.
the combination of different stress conditions in SSF processes can be successfully managed by using the right strain, and by supplementing it with low-cost nutrients.
